claim: Beckmeyer, Branger and Gayda find retail investors lost $241,000 on an average day in S&P 500 0DTE options between February 2021 and September 2023, and $350,000 per day since daily expirations began in May 2022.

evidence.quote: retail investors together lost more than $125 million. More than $90 million of these losses are the result of the transaction costs, the remainder a result of poor positioning

claim: The same paper attributes the losses to single-leg trades, trades requiring an upfront payment and trades in high-implied-volatility options.
